name: The hub runs one input per command
problem: The hub can be run from a command line one input at a time, and each run starts without the earlier ones, so a person cannot try it or steer it by talking with it, answer a question it asks, or see what it is doing between one line and the next.
who_has_it: People trying the hub or working with it from a terminal.
why_it_matters: A person who cannot converse with the hub tries fewer inputs, answers its questions late or not at all, and judges it on one reply.
why_hard: A conversation needs the work, the questions and the commands drawn as they happen, and the same front door a script uses, so the session cannot reach into the hub's parts.
existing_attempts: A one-shot command per input, and scripts that call the front door in a loop; neither draws the work or a question for a person to answer.

name: The same update is shown twice while the AI works
problem: While a run is in progress the same update appears at the bottom and at the top of the terminal: in the full-screen arm each finished step, helper and queued message was written to the transcript and kept in the live panel, and in the reference terminal a row wider than the screen wrapped, so the in-place redraw erased too few rows and left the previous frame above the new one.
who_has_it: People watching an AI run from a terminal.
why_it_matters: A person reads the same line twice, cannot tell whether it happened twice, and loses the one place to look for what is happening now.
why_hard: Two regions share one stream of events, and the screen's real width and height are known only to the terminal, so a frame that fits on paper can still wrap or overflow and break the redraw.
existing_attempts: Hiding one of the two regions, which loses either the live view or the record.

name: Every app rebuilds the terminal rules people settled on
problem: An app that polishes its terminal over many rounds of use ends with rules the hub's thin screen does not have: a note typed while the AI works is queued, counted and sent as one next message, a stopped run flushes it and a failed one does not, one closing line comes from structured fields, warnings fold to one line with the rest in a file, a clock shows at every wait over three seconds, the prompt stays at the bottom and everything fits 80 columns. The next app, and the hub's own screen, start again from none of it.
who_has_it: People who work with an AI in a terminal built on the hub, and the teams that build those terminals.
why_it_matters: Each rule was a complaint once. A screen without them loses a typed note, shows two clocks, hides a stop, or buries the work under warnings, and a person stops trusting what it says.
why_hard: The rules are small, many and interact (the queue, the question, the stop and the error each change what happens to a note), so they are found by use and lost when a screen is rewritten; the generic ones are tangled in one app's own objects.
existing_attempts: Rewriting the rules in each app; a thin hub screen that leaves them out.
